title: Outer-2 real-SWAP participant admissibility boundary at the solver-configuration split

technical_history.repair: Keep the exact frozen NOUR/G17/STANDARD binary64 heads as primary authority and report their binary64-derived separation instead of treating a one-ulp-inconsistent redundant derived field as an independent gate. No status, scan, physics or acceptance rule changed.

boundary_refinement.reason: The preregistered coarse topology is nonmonotone with five transitions and two 0-to-6 reversals, so a single threshold/bisection claim is forbidden.

bounded_conclusions: The G21E NOUR/G17 outer-2 status difference is not a single narrow monotone participant threshold. Across only 1.9795e-13 m, equivalent to 1783 binary64 ulps at this head, the 33-point frozen scan contains five status transitions and two reversals.
The local topology therefore contains alternating status-6 and status-0 islands. A one-ulp boundary, head snapping rule or acceptance tolerance cannot be inferred from this evidence.
The persisted anchors reproduce exactly: the NOUR head is status 6, while the G17 and STANDARD heads are status 0.

At the NOUR status-6 anchor the trial fails with result_status 2 after nine attempts, eight temporal rejections and one solver rejection, with no accepted substeps. At the status-0 G17 and STANDARD anchors the participant completes 20 accepted substeps after 100 attempts and 80 temporal rejections, with zero solver rejection.

Mass rejection and temporal-unavailable rejection remain zero at both sides. The immediate observed discriminator at the anchor level is therefore solver failure after a retry sequence, but G21F does not yet identify the source-level numerical mechanism that creates the nonmonotone status islands.
Because the coarse topology is nonmonotone, the preregistered binary64 bisection and repeated adjacent-endpoint sessions are correctly not executed.
All observations remain diagnostic through G16: no live candidate, accepted revision/time, committed ledger or publication preflight authority is acquired.
This result further weakens any attempt to interpret strict G17 trajectory fidelity as a smooth head-space robustness metric or to select STANDARD/NOUR from the single frozen carrier.
next_natural_unit: Open a source-level causal diagnostic of the alternating status-0/status-6 islands. Freeze representative heads from each coarse island, inspect per-attempt temporal-step/retry/solver outcomes and the exact rejection site in the real FMR/SWAP corrector, and test whether the islands are caused by temporal step-size/retry bifurcation, solver convergence state, or another discrete execution branch. Do not smooth or alter participant acceptance.
